newsitem.title: IRAN: Iranian envoy to sue paper over defection article.
newsitem.headline: Iranian envoy to sue paper over defection article.

text.p: Iran's former envoy to Tajikistan is planning to sue a local weekly for reporting he had defected and sought political asylum, the official news agencuy IRNA said on Sunday.
Ali Ashraf Shabestari said he would file a law suit against Kayhan Havaie, the weekly publication of the Kayhan newspapers group, it added.
He said claims by the weekly's managing director that he had joined the outlawed Mujahideen Khalq Organisation tarnished his image as well as that of the Islamic republic.
He said "such unfounded claims stem from personal grudge".
Shabestari, who returned to Tehran recently after five years as envoy to Tajikistan, now heads the international economic affairs department at the foreign ministry, it said.

An Iranian opposition group said last week Shabestari and at least three other Iranian diplomats -- one from the mission in Pakistan and two others in European embassies -- had defected and sought asylum abroad.
Tehran denied the report and said enemies of Iran were spreading rumours of defections to harm its image.

The Paris-based Council of Resistance of Iran identified Shabestari as ambassador to Tajikistan and said Tehran had sent a mission from the ministry of intelligence to Europe to review personnel at each embassy.
It did not say where diplomats had sought asylum in Europe.
